name: Kaisers
kurzbeschreibung: Highest village in the Außerfern, surrounded by lush alpine meadows and the breathtaking Kaisertal.
beschreibung:
Overview

Kaisers is situated at an altitude of 1,518 metres in a secluded high-altitude valley of the upper Lechtal in the district of Reutte. Cradled between the rugged limestone crests of the Lechtal Alps where the Almajur Valley merges into the Kaiser Valley, this mountain municipality counts only about 75 residents. Consequently, Kaisers holds the distinction of being the smallest municipality by population in the entire province of Tyrol, as well as the most sparsely populated community in Austria, with an average density of just one person per square kilometre. As an official Mountaineering Village (Bergsteigerdorf) of the Alpine Clubs, Kaisers is purely dedicated to gentle, non-commercial alpine pursuits. Visitors are greeted by raw alpine nature, ancient sun-blackened timber chalets, and profound tranquility far from mass tourism.

History

Initial colonization began during the 13th century when alpine dairy farmsteads (Schwaighöfe) were established across the 2,310-metre Kaiserjoch pass from the Stanzertal near Landeck. The first written documentation of cheese levies from the area dates to 1275 in a Landeck court tax registry, while the actual name was recorded on February 6, 1385, referring to people living "in Kaiser". Over centuries, villagers maintained close kinship and trade bonds with Walser and Alemannic communities across the Arlberg and Tannberg mountains. Devastating fires swept the village in 1833 and 1851, destroying many ancient structures. The heritage-protected Parish Church of St. Anne was rebuilt in historicist style following the 1851 blaze, its slender bell tower standing as the scenic heart of the high-altitude settlement.

Getting There

Kaisers is reached via an adventurous alpine mountain road. Motorists from Germany can travel toll-free via the A7 motorway past Füssen or Reutte, following the B198 Lechtal federal highway through the valley to Steeg. In Steeg, the winding L268 provincial road climbs steeply for four kilometres through switchbacks directly into Kaisers. During snow-free summer months, scenic access is also open from Vorarlberg via Warth and Steeg. Train travellers arrive at Reutte in Tirol or Füssen stations, connecting with regional bus route 110 into Steeg, where scheduled valley shuttle vans and taxi services provide connections up to Kaisers.

Tips

Kaisers is a premier launching point for wilderness trekking across the Lechtal Alps. A classic alpine excursion ascends through the Kaisertal valley to the historic Kaiserjochhaus mountain hut at 2,310 metres, commanding dramatic views across the Stanzertal and providing trail access to Mount Stanskogel (2,757 m). The serene Almajur Valley south of the village invites hikers and mountain bikers to visit the traditional pastures of Bodenalpe and Erlachalpe. In the village, the DAV Edelweißhaus serves as a welcoming mountain lodge for long-distance trekkers along the Lechtal High Trail and for backcountry ski tourers during winter.
